about: cove(from_at, to_at, lumens, kelvin, ledge, out, wall) runs one level ledge along a wall, from `from_at` to `to_at` (points on the wall's face at the ledge's top; the line runs along x or along z). The ledge is 0.1 m deep and 0.04 m thick, its softened front edge carries an upstand 0.06 m high and 0.02 m thick. Behind the upstand, on the ledge, lies a strip of light facing up: it washes the wall and the ceiling above and is never seen from below. `out` says which way the ledge leaves the wall: -1 is towards -z for a line along x and towards -x for a line along z; 1 is the other way. With `wall` above 0 a plaster wall that high stands behind it (0.3 m of it below the ledge), for a bare picture; in a room leave it 0. Gives back the strip's glowing rectangle.
licence: our own work, free for every J Production project
name: cove
place: cove(AT + vec(-1.5, 0.4, 0), AT + vec(1.5, 0.4, 0), lumens: 600, kelvin: 2700, out: 1, wall: 1.4)
what: a plaster ledge on a wall with a strip of light hidden on top

The light's angle is the dome's opening, so the dome owns the pool below and nothing leaves upward. Gives back the light.
licence: our own work, free for every J Production project
name: pendant_dome
what: a plain metal dome on a cord, its light falling in a cone

about: use "human" brings it in; bones("human", at: vec(0, 0, 0)) shows it standing. An adult 1.75 m tall in the rest pose: facing -z, left at -x, arms 45 degrees down and out, palms down. Each bone says where it starts and ends, the way a positive bend carries its tip, and how far it turns from rest: bend, side, twist. A turn not named does not happen (an elbow never bends sideways). Every left_ bone gets its right_ twin; on the right, side and twist run the other way. Rings 2 (the bones that follow) and 3 (the face) come after.
credit: J Production, made in Loop3D. Proportions after Drillis and Contini (1966) and Winter, Biomechanics and Motor Control of Human Movement. Joint limits after the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons, Joint Motion: Method of Measuring and Recording (1965), and Norkin and White, Measurement of Joint Motion; rounded, and shared along the spine and neck
licence: our own work, free for every J Production project (the measurements are published facts)
name: human
what: the standard human skeleton, ring 1: the 66 bones you move

about: city_night(toward, eye_height, seed, lit, at, lamp) puts a dark blue-black sky with a few stars, a haze that fades far towers to blue, and 180 lit-window towers in a fan 60 degrees each side of `toward` (towards -z by default): 40 from 120 to 250 m away, 60 from 300 to 600 m, 80 from 800 to 1,500 m, none nearer than 100 m, their feet `eye_height` below `at` (the eye, the middle of the glass). Under them a dark street and, far out at 300 m, a low panel of dull orange (the streets' glow). One tall group stands off-centre and one stretch of sky is left clear; each seed puts them elsewhere. `toward` leans to -z (its z is negative). It adds ONE lamp outside, a cool panel the size of a 9 by 6 m window, 1 m outside the glass facing in (the city's own light reaching the room: 7,500 K, 300 lumens, no shadows). It is the only lamp outside; `lamp: no` leaves it out (the panel shines at the eye from the glass side). Gives back that light.
licence: our own work, free for every J Production project
name: city_night
what: the city at night in three depths, seen from forty metres up
